analysis:
Look at evidence hard.

Contract asserts on side effects: file created by redirect, file absent after Ctrl-C, vim `:wq` writing file, `~/.bashrc` export visible in fresh terminal, background `&` job serving HTTP after 5s.

Failures a1/a6/a7/a8 vs passes a2/a3/a4/a5/a9/a10 — checked every candidate discriminator:

- shell flags: `-i` vs `-i -l` — both sides both ways (a2 passes with `-l`)
- pyte vs raw buffer — both sides both ways (a5/a9/a10 pyte, pass)
- kill signal on close — mixed
- honoring `wait_sec` vs early idle-settle break — only a6 clearly breaks it (matters for background-job test), not the other three
- bashrc verification — a7 did real `/root/.bashrc` marker test and still failed; a5/a9 skipped it and passed

No single mechanism spans the four fails. Fixes differ per attempt (one is wait-semantics, others are elsewhere). Rule 2 fires.

Closest coherent class me could name — "failers verified via convenient stand-in (interactive-flag echo, `$HOME` echo, temp-HOME rc, `less` instead of real editor) instead of real trigger path" — is the reproduction category already killed at gate as R3 (`976ba00fdcc55467`, 6/10 vs 3/10, negative direction). Rule 8 forbids re-deriving.
